html:
Eswatini, called Swaziland until 2018, is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, between South Africa and Mozambique. The map shows it under the name Swaziland from 1880 to the present.

The Swazi kingdom took shape in the mid-1700s under King Ngwane III, whose name the country also bears. In the early 1800s King Sobhuza I moved north to escape pressure from the growing Zulu kingdom and gathered other clans under his rule. His son Mswati II, from whom the Swazi take their name, built a strong army and expanded the kingdom.

In the late 1800s Swazi kings sold so many land and mineral concessions to whites that they lost control over much of the country. It came under the Transvaal in 1894 and, after the Boer War, became a British protectorate. Unlike its neighbours Lesotho and Botswana, it was never fully absorbed into South Africa.

Swaziland became independent in 1968 under King Sobhuza II, who in 1973 banned political parties and ruled directly; his reign of over 82 years is among the longest known. His son Mswati III has ruled since 1986, one of the last absolute monarchs in the world. Eswatini has had one of the world's highest rates of HIV infection.
